name: Hong Kong
description: Victoria Harbour from open data: Central, Admiralty and Wan Chai, Tsim Sha Tsui and the Peak, every building at the height the Lands Department surveyed, on the government's LiDAR terrain and under the real sun.

imagery.attribution: Aerial photograph from Lands Department, (c) The Government of the Hong Kong SAR, through the Lands Department Map API (GeoData Store)

terrain.attribution: Civil Engineering and Development Department, territory-wide airborne LiDAR digital terrain model, 0.5 m, flown December 2019 to February 2020; Hong Kong 1980 Grid, mPD (CSDI, (c) The Government of the Hong Kong SAR)

surface_check.name: CEDD territory-wide airborne LiDAR digital surface model, 0.5 m, flown December 2019 to February 2020
surface_check.flown: 20 December 2019 to 2 February 2020, by helicopter (CSDI dataset record)

survey.attribution: Lands Department, Building dataset (building block outlines with surveyed top and base levels in mPD, and storeys), CSDI portal, (c) The Government of the Hong Kong SAR

water.note: Victoria Harbour is OpenStreetMap's coastline polygon (Overture 'ocean') plus the typhoon shelters. Water is drawn at 0 mPD, about the lowest tide: mean sea level is about 1.3 mPD.

waves.note: The prevailing easterly blowing down the harbour from Lei Yue Mun, over about 6 km of open water, 12-15 m deep. Chosen values, not a measurement; the harbour's real chop comes as much from ferry wakes.

water.colour_note: Victoria Harbour is green-grey and turbid, with a couple of metres of visibility; colours picked from the Lands Department aerial photo.

game.title: Hong Kong on Foot

wharves.name: Tsim Sha Tsui
wharves.terminal: 尖沙咀天星碼頭 Tsim Sha Tsui Star Ferry Pier

wharves.name: Wan Chai
wharves.terminal: 灣仔碼頭 Wan Chai Pier

game.ferry_note: Piers, berths and the heliport are from OpenStreetMap via Overture. The Star Ferry's two routes are real; the vessel names are from its fleet, but which vessel runs which route, and the timetable, are not. Ferries run at 1.5 times their service speed and wait 20 s at each pier. At a pier you can skip the wait.

ferry_style.note: The Star Ferry's green hull and white upper deck; the dimensions are approximate.

helipads.name: Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre heliport

tram.note: Hong Kong Tramways' double-deck cars on the tracks OpenStreetMap maps. A car is about 8.9 m long, 2.0 m wide and 4.5 m tall (CPTDB; a 1967 report gives 29 ft by 14 ft 9 in); the running speed and stop spacing are approximate, the colours a mix of the green livery and advertising wraps.

funicular.name: Peak Tram
funicular.note: 1,277 m of track climbing 358 m since the 2022 rebuild, at 6 m/s (Peak Tramways via ropeways.net); the line is the one OpenStreetMap maps, on the LiDAR terrain. The car is about 33 m long (the 2018 plan); its width is a guess.

npcs.name: Ka-yan
idle: Every building here has a surveyed top level from the Lands Department, and a LiDAR scan from 2020 to check it against. Not many cities can say that.

npcs.name: Wing
idle: A survey says how tall a building is. A laser says how tall it looked from a helicopter in January 2020. When they disagree, one of them is out of date.

npcs.name: Mr Leung
idle: Central to Tsim Sha Tsui, about a kilometre of harbour. Mind the gangway.

npcs.name: Grace
idle: The International Commerce Centre tops out at 484 m. Give it a wide berth.

npcs.name: Mei
idle: Hong Kong has no rule that protects the sun on its squares. The planning guidelines protect a view instead: a band of green below the Peak's ridgeline, seen from the harbour.

npcs.name: Ah Keung
idle: Ding ding! The trams have run along this shore since 1904. The sea used to come right up to Des Voeux Road.

npcs.name: Siu-man
idle: The Peak Tram climbs some 360 metres from Garden Road. Stand at the back and the towers lean the wrong way.

quests.title: Across the harbour
talk: You're the new surveyor? Good. This is Victoria Harbour from open data: {buildings} buildings, almost every one at the height the Lands Department surveyed, on the government's own LiDAR terrain.
Take the Star Ferry over to Tsim Sha Tsui. Wing is waiting by the Clock Tower.
WASD or the arrow keys to move, Shift to sprint, X to walk, drag to look around. E to talk, or to wait for the ferry.

steps.text: Take the Star Ferry from Central to Tsim Sha Tsui
Meet Wing at the Clock Tower

quests.title: Two measurements
talk: {share:survey}% of the footprint area has a surveyed top level, and {share:lidar}% is measured from the 2020 LiDAR scan where the survey falls short. Only {share:estimate}% is estimated.
Aim at a building and press Q to use the survey lens. Find one with a surveyed height and one measured by LiDAR.
Then take the ferry to Wan Chai. Grace keeps a helicopter at the Convention Centre.

steps.text: Survey lens (Q): a surveyed and a LiDAR-measured height
Take the Star Ferry from Tsim Sha Tsui to Wan Chai
Meet Grace at the Convention Centre heliport

quests.title: Between the towers
talk: Ready? Two IFC stands 412 m on the Central waterfront, and the ICC 484 m across the water. Both are in the model at their surveyed tops.
Fly west along the shore and set down in Tamar Park, by the Government Headquarters. Mei will meet you in Statue Square.
Space to climb, C to descend, W and S for forward and back, A and D to turn. V switches to a bird's-eye view. E gets you out once you've landed.

quests.title: Winter sun on Statue Square
talk: Statue Square sits among the bank towers: HSBC to the south, the Bank of China behind it. At midwinter the sun is only 44° up at noon, and it comes from the south, over them.
On 21 December at noon, {sun:Statue Square|12-21|12:00}% of the square is in direct sun. Go and find a sunny spot.
Nothing in Hong Kong's rules protects that sun. The model can still measure it.

steps.text: Stand in direct sun in Statue Square, 11:00 to 14:00 on 21 December
Find Siu-man at the Peak Tram's Garden Road terminus

quests.title: Up the Peak
talk: The Peak Tram has climbed from Garden Road to the Peak since 1888. The line here is the one OpenStreetMap maps, laid on the LiDAR terrain.
Ride it to the top. Mrs Fong is up there every evening; she'll show you the view.

steps.text: Ride the Peak Tram from Garden Road to the Peak
Find Mrs Fong at the lookout by the Peak Tram terminus

quests.title: The view
talk: That's the whole harbour: the ferry, the towers, the trams and the hill.
Every height you can see has a source, and {lidar:within_2m_pct}% of the surveyed roofs agree with the laser to within 2 m.
Stay for the evening. At eight the towers light up for the Symphony of Lights.

reference_heights.source: Wikipedia, List of tallest buildings in Hong Kong (accessed 28 October 2026), with its coordinates; buildings of 180 m and more inside the model

terrain_check.name: Lands Department Geodetic Survey Control Station Database: levelling bench marks, mPD (CSDI)
terrain_check.note: Bench marks are staples and rods set in kerbs, walls and steps, levelled to the Hong Kong Principal Datum; the traverse stations in the same database mostly carry no levelled height (0), so they are not used.

tour.title: Victoria Harbour from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings from OpenStreetMap and the Lands Department, standing on the government's 2020 LiDAR terrain under the real sun. {share:survey}% of the footprint area has a surveyed top level, and {share:lidar}% more is measured from the LiDAR.

tour.title: Heights you can check
tour.text: Blue is a measured height. The Lands Department surveys the top level of every building block; where its blocks miss a footprint, the 2020 LiDAR scan measures the roof. Against the laser, the surveyed roofs agree to {lidar:median_abs_m} m at the median; against the published list of tallest buildings, to {acc:median_abs_error_pct}%.

tour.title: Bank of China Tower
tour.text: I. M. Pei's tower is a 52 m square cut along its diagonals into four triangular shafts that stop at four heights, the lowest on the harbour side, the last at the 315 m roof. Its faces are turned {landmark:bank_of_china.bearing_deg}° from north, measured on its footprint. The masts reach 367.4 m.

tour.title: Statue Square at midwinter
tour.text: On 21 December the noon sun stands 44° above the southern horizon, behind the bank towers. {sun:Statue Square|12-21|12:00}% of Statue Square is in direct sun at noon. Hong Kong has no rule that protects the sun on its public squares; the model can still measure it.

tour.title: The Star Ferry crossing
tour.text: About a kilometre of harbour between Central's Pier 7 and Tsim Sha Tsui. The water moves with an easterly blowing down the harbour; the piers and the shoreline are OpenStreetMap's.

tour.title: Two IFC and the ICC
tour.text: The two tallest buildings in the model face each other across the harbour: Two IFC at 412 m and the ICC at 484 m, built to their published heights and crowns. The Lands Department's survey puts their main roofs 11 m and 1 m from those figures.

tour.title: The Peak at dusk
tour.text: The Peak Tram climbs some 360 m from Garden Road to the Peak Tower, whose crescent roof stands 428 m above the datum. After dark the towers' windows light up across the water.

light_show.name: A Symphony of Lights
light_show.note: A Symphony of Lights has run at 8 pm nightly since 2004, with lights on some 40 buildings on both sides of the harbour (Wikipedia; Tourism Commission). In February 2026 the government said it would be retired in the second half of 2026 (Hong Kong Free Press, 27 February 2026); it was still running in September. The beams, lasers and colours here are illustrative, not the show's choreography.
